slides.title: Bored or Boring?

runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these five things.
I can say how something was.
It was exciting. / It was boring.
I can say how I felt: I was excited.
I can give an opinion with a reason.
I can read reviews and write a review.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: It was exciting. / It was boring. Goal 2: I was excited. / I was bored. Goal 3: -ing (the thing, the experience) or -ed (the person's feeling).
Goal 4: I thought it was confusing, so I left early. Goal 5: read three short reviews and write a 3–4 sentence review with stars.
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check. It is not a test grade.
Lesson plan: At a glance: Objectives.

runs.t: I was bored, so I left early.

slides.notes:
"Say it" (2 min). Say: "-ed has 3 sounds." Read: relaxed (t), bored (d), interested (id, one more syllable). The class repeats each word twice. Then the line in the box.
-ed sounds: /t/ after x, k, s, sh, ch, p (relaxed); /id/ after t, d (interested, one more syllable); /d/ for the rest (bored, tired, surprised). Don't teach the rule; just model and repeat.

Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Star Ratings · 12 min.
Round 1 (7 min): each learner chooses an event card (1–6) or a real event (a TV show or a sports game is fine). A tells B about it: how it was, how they felt, and one reason. B asks two follow-up questions and gives it 1–5 stars in the table. Switch. Each click shows the next step.

slides.notes:
Step 6 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP.
Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one with -ing and one with -ed about the same event, and a reason with because or so (The concert was exciting, so I was excited all night.). Collect at the door.
Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (one sentence on the board). Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."
Homework items: 1 write the sentence with -ing or -ed • 2 an event, a movie, or a game from this month: 3 sentences (how it was, how you felt, and why) • 3 ask a family member or a coworker: What was the best event or movie this year? Why? • 4 review (Lesson 10): 3 steps for making a cup of coffee or tea with First, Then, Finally.
Read & Write (7:17–7:25, on the Student Pages): three short reviews; questions 1–5; then a 3–4 sentence review with 1–5 stars and one reason. If behind: questions 1–5 only; the review becomes homework.

slides.title: Before You Go

runs.t: I can say how something was (It was interesting).
I can say how I felt (I was interested).
I can give an opinion with a reason.
I can write a short review.
A. Listen to the teacher. Circle a or b.
a. The concert was not fun.   b. The concert was fun.
a. It was surprising.   b. I felt surprised.
a. I liked the museum.   b. I didn't like the museum.
a. They stayed until the end.   b. They left because they were tired.

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle a or b. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "The concert was boring." (a) • 2 "I was surprised." (b) • 3 "The museum was interesting." (a) • 4 "We were tired, so we left." (b)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 exciting, 2 bored, 3 confusing, 4 relaxed. C: answers will vary (for example The festival was exciting. I was excited. / I thought it was boring, so I left early.).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the endings (A) and choosing -ing / -ed (B, C).
Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 13). If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 13 at 6:00, while learners arrive.
Lesson plan: Progress Check step; Progress Check page; Answer key.
